findings: Daily limit validation uses no guard for null card — calculateDailySpent() is called only if card != null (protected by APPROVED status check), but during daily limit logic, card is already confirmed non-null. Not an issue in practice but logic is correct; no action required.

Decline reason codes in manual operations unvalidated — When manually declining via PUT /decline, the reason string is stored directly as declineReasonCode without validation. A very long reason string could theoretically exceed VARCHAR(50). Consider truncating or validating reason length in a follow-up if manual operations are user-input facing.

Legacy method still processes new cardNumber parameter — Controller passes cardNumber to createAuthorizationWithAutoApproval(), which accepts it. The service prefers cardId-based lookup. If a card is not found by ID but cardNumber is provided, the service still uses that cardNumber in the Authorization entity. This is correct behavior, but verify cardNumber is consistently populated in all code paths.
